description.narrative: (South Sudan): . ..In FY 2018, the Integrated Essential Emergency Education Services Project (IEEES) continues to provide protection, education and learning opportunities to those most negatively impacted by South Sudan's conflict. USAID will support out-of-school, internally displaced persons (IDP) and host-community children and youth to achieve measurable outcomes in reading and psychosocial well-being with interventions that increase equitable access to safe learning environments and improve instruction in essential life skills. UNICEF is the prime partner for this activity as it is one of the only organizations able to access conflict-prone areas, where beneficiaries have the most need. This makes UNICEF well suited to implement in South Sudan. Due to ongoing security threats and logistical challenges since conflict erupted in 2013, USAID/South Sudan has shifted to partner more with UN agencies, which are often the only organizations able to access key program locations due to their ability to utilize assets of and coordinate with the United Nations Mission in South Sudan peacekeeping operations..... .

title.narrative: Integrated Emergency Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Response and Prevention of Gender Based Violence (GBV)

description.narrative: (South Sudan): .Through this activity, USAID provides access to basic water, sanitation, and hygiene services; mitigates risks of gender-based violence (GBV) for women and girls; and provides life-saving services related to GBV, including addressing psychosocial needs in South Sudan. With FY 2019 funds, USAID will improve the health of 100,000 South Sudanese with access to basic water and sanitation services by: 1) promoting positive hygiene and sanitation practices; 2) expanding access to basic safe water and sanitation, and 3) supporting and strengthening the capacity of local authorities and communities to plan, implement, and govern water and sanitation services. GBV prevention and response will be an integral part of all the activities. FY 2019 funds will be used to:.Increase access to basic safe water by rehabilitating 80 non-functional boreholes; drilling 45 new boreholes; building five water yards with solar systems; and training Water Management Committee members.Improve access to basic sanitation services by constructing 12 communal latrines in high-population locations; working with 12 villages to trigger Community-Led Total Sanitation (CLTS); conduct capacity-building sessions in latrine construction; and supply tools and materials for constructing latrines.Promote integrated social behavior change hygiene messages through a trained network of volunteers and sanitation promotion activities, including menstrual hygiene management at schools and public settings. This activity was awarded to IOM because of its organizational flexibility and consistent presence on the ground in South Sudan despite outbreaks of conflict. IOM's experience in working in the implementation areas and with targeted communities as well as its close collaboration with UN organizations and the UN Mission's response in Protection of Civilians sites makes IOM uniquely suited to implement the WASH activities.
